title: Reverse the List
problem: The first line of input is a positive integer N. The second line holds N integers separated by spaces. Print the same numbers in reverse order, on one line, separated by single spaces. For example, 1 2 3 becomes 3 2 1.
starter_code:
# The first line is N, the count of numbers.
# The second line holds N integers separated by spaces.
# Print them in reverse order, separated by spaces.

# Write your code here

hints.1: Read the numbers into a list first, then think about walking through it from the back.
hints.2: Use input().split() to get a list of the numbers, reverse the list (not the text of the line), then print it with ' '.join(...). Reversing the whole line as text would also flip the digits inside each number.

failure_explanation: Reverse the order of the numbers, not the characters of the line: reversing the text turns the digits of a longer number around as well. Print the result as numbers separated by single spaces, not as a Python list with brackets and commas.
